assessment_summary: The statement is mathematically false. While Grötzsch's theorem states that every *planar* triangle-free graph is 3-colorable, the unrestricted statement is false. Triangle-free graphs can have arbitrarily large chromatic numbers, as demonstrated by the Mycielskian construction. Therefore, any attempt to prove the statement will inevitably fail to justify that a 3-coloring can always be completed or that a vertex of degree < 3 always exists.
counterexample: The Grötzsch graph (the Mycielskian of the 5-cycle) is a finite, simple, triangle-free graph that has a chromatic number of 4, so it cannot be properly colored with 3 colors.
